correctness.rationale: Let \(e_j=F(j/N)\) and \(m=\min_j e_j\). Exact decision preservation forces the first \(k\) values to be at least \(1/\alpha\), while every tail value is at least \(m\). Exact e-validity on the uniform rank grid gives \(N=\sum_j e_j\ge k/\alpha+(N-k)m\), hence the stated \(m^*\). Equality forces every head value to equal \(1/\alpha\) and every tail value to equal the common minimum, so the optimizer is unique on the grid. When \(\alpha N\) is integral, the first \(k\) values already exhaust the total expectation, forcing every tail value to zero. The bundled rational checker validates representative lattice and nonlattice cases; the theorem itself is the exact normalization argument.
residual_risks: The theorem assumes the tie-free uniform conformal rank grid and optimizes only the worst-rank floor.
